items.note: It answers the question directly ("Likely yes"). It backs this with Pro churn before and after the increase, using Basic as a comparison. The numbers match the data: 1/23 vs 10/46 for Pro, 1/24 vs 3/49 for Basic.
It excludes the 15 trial rows, which is the correct count, and says it did.
It excludes the 5 @ourco.test accounts and notes they would have added 5 false August Pro churns.
It counts churn as having a cancel_month, recorded in that month. The counts are correct: 11 non-trial, non-QA Pro churns in total, 10 of them from July onward.

It isn't pitched at a CEO. The answer opens with a six-row data-quality table, account IDs and assumptions. Even the CEO bullets use analyst terms like "logo churn" and "account-months" and give several rates per bullet. The CEO-facing message is buried in a technical report.
The section labelled for the CEO has exactly 5 bullets. But the output as a whole is a long report with many tables and dozens of extra bullets. That is far beyond a summary of at most 5 bullets.
It suggests one chart: monthly churn rate for Pro and Basic, with a line marking July and counts on each point.

It rates confidence "Low-to-moderate" and ties that explicitly to the small sample (20 Pro accounts, 10 post-increase churns). It separates being confident about the direction from being unsure about the size of the effect.
